facts.text: Phil Spector worked on the Beatles' Let It Be and produced some of John Lennon's solo albums, their relationship deteriorating and ending by the 1974 recording of Rock'n'Roll.

On 2003-02-03, actress Lana Clarkson was found shot dead at Phil Spector's Hollywood mansion; he was charged with murder, arrested on 2003-02-04 and released on $1m bail.
On 2003-09-22, the Los Angeles coroner's office ruled Lana Clarkson's death at Phil Spector's home a homicide, contradicting Spector's claim that she committed suicide.
On 2004-09-27, Phil Spector pleaded not guilty to murder after being indicted in connection with the death of actor Lana Clarkson.
Phil Spector's murder trial ran in 2007: jury selection began 2007-03-19, the trial opened 2007-04-25, and the jury declared itself deadlocked on 2007-09-18, ending in a mistrial on 2007-09-26.
On 2008-10-24, Phil Spector gave his first lengthy television interview for a BBC2 documentary, protesting his innocence in Lana Clarkson's death and comparing his work to Leonardo da Vinci.

In July 2000 a court awarded the Ronettes $2.6 million in royalties dating back to 1963 after lengthy litigation with Phil Spector; on 2001-11-15 an appeal court ordered him to pay $3 million for unpaid royalties.
In August 2002, Phil Spector came out of two decades of retirement to record two tracks with the band Starsailor and was discussing producing their next album.
On 2003-02-03, actress Lana Clarkson was found shot dead at Phil Spector's Hollywood mansion; he was charged with murder, arrested on 2003-02-04 and released on $1m bail.
On 2003-09-22, the Los Angeles coroner's office ruled Lana Clarkson's death at Phil Spector's home a homicide, contradicting Spector's claim that she committed suicide.
On 2004-09-27, Phil Spector pleaded not guilty to murder after being indicted in connection with the death of actor Lana Clarkson.
Phil Spector's 2007 murder trial: jury selection began 2007-03-19, the trial opened 2007-04-25, the jury declared itself deadlocked on 2007-09-18, and a mistrial was declared on 2007-09-26.

On 2007-05-09, two more women testified at Phil Spector's murder trial that he threatened them with guns, bringing to four the number of prosecution witnesses describing a pattern of gun threats before the 2003 death of Lana Clarkson.

facts.text: Phil Spector worked on the Beatles' Let It Be and produced some of John Lennon's solo albums, their relationship deteriorating and ending by the 1974 recording of Rock'n'Roll.

On 2003-09-22, the Los Angeles coroner's office ruled Lana Clarkson's death at Phil Spector's home a homicide, contradicting Spector's claim that she committed suicide.
On 2003-11-14, the Beatles' album Let It Be... Naked was released, presenting a version of Let It Be closer to the band's original intentions and removing Phil Spector's production.
On 2004-09-27, Phil Spector pleaded not guilty to murder after being indicted in connection with the death of actor Lana Clarkson.

facts.text: Phil Spector worked on the Beatles' Let It Be and produced some of John Lennon's solo albums, their relationship deteriorating and ending by the 1974 recording of Rock'n'Roll.

In August 2002, Phil Spector came out of two decades of retirement to record two tracks with the band Starsailor and was discussing producing their next album.
On 2003-02-03, actress Lana Clarkson was found shot dead at Phil Spector's Hollywood mansion; he was charged with murder, arrested on 2003-02-04 and released on $1m bail.
On 2003-02-13, Phil Spector's friend said his defense would claim the fatal shooting of actress Lana Clarkson at his home was an accident.
On 2003-09-22, the Los Angeles coroner's office ruled Lana Clarkson's death at Phil Spector's home a homicide, contradicting Spector's claim that she committed suicide.
On 2004-09-27, Phil Spector pleaded not guilty to murder after being indicted in connection with the death of actor Lana Clarkson.
On 2007-04-26, in Phil Spector's murder trial, a former girlfriend testified that he threatened her with a revolver and a shotgun during a 1993 encounter.
